overview: A Pacific storm brings snow to Utah and the northern Rockies through Friday and Saturday, then a weaker system follows Monday. The central Rockies get snow showers Friday into Saturday, and the WPC expects more wet systems over the West into midweek.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A Pacific storm system brings snow to Utah's mountains through early Saturday, focused increasingly on northern Utah. Powder Mountain is the top resort, with a 10 inch total and 9 inches on Friday. The NWS is calling for more, 12 to 20 inches over Friday through Monday. A Winter Storm Warning runs from Thursday night to Saturday. Dry weather returns for the weekend before a weaker system hits Monday.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Snow rates pick up Thursday night into Friday, with the heaviest totals for the mountains west of the Divide. Grand Targhee is the top resort, with a 10 inch total and 6 inches on Friday. Snow then shifts east Friday afternoon, bringing snow to southern and central Wyoming and possible travel trouble on I-80. A Winter Weather Advisory covers the area through Friday night, and the weekend stays unsettled and cold.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Snow showers move across the Colorado and Utah high country tonight into Saturday, with a possible snow squall near US 40 and I-70 Friday morning. Telluride is the top resort, with a 7 inch total. Shower activity drops off Saturday, then picks up again Sunday night and Monday with a stronger cold push.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
